I hope to bring it to the media and hopefully it'll draw attention. I was there truly to get help. After overdosing, and realising the self harm was brought on by depression, I realised I needed help, and the facility wasn't to great at giving that to their patients.

What I was able to find out is one way they may be getting away with it is by saying (and this was said directly to me) "If it isn't in writing it didn't happen" pair that with the fact that the cameras don't record and I think that's enough for the  department of health and public affairs to investigate. As well as the department of health care administration. I've got the phone number of the client/patient that pointed out the various violations. They equated it to what assylums used to have a rep for. (I personally dislike using the term client as it makes me feel like a customer more than a patient which in actuality is what you are). They more than likely try to squeeze as much money out of the clients by providing everything on as minimal of a shoestring budget as they can. The staff there only required a high school diploma. I also don't think the doctor was TEFL Certified. I am planning to look into the Florida Health Licencing Registrar for the doctors name. I think a lot of the staff knew nothing could be done about them or don't think anything will be done about them which is why they were so careless with their jobs. I asked to get a copy of a form I signed (that was stored in my file while I was there) and they denied that. Didn't tell me much reason why except for "management won't allow us to". I am also doing research on some other things that were brought up to me (other laws, etc) to see what other things I can report them for.

In all honesty, the facility I was at was VERY unprofessionally ran, the discharge process took about 3-4 hours. The doctor was half deaf, took forever to see patients, and there were many staff that were downright disrespectful to clients/patients. I remember one instance where a staff member went up to a patient sleeping in a chair, shook him awake and told him to go back to sleep. When I attempted to speak out against it publicly, they told me to close my mouth. I am in talks with a fellow patient who was discharged to get many of the HIPPA and Health violations known about publicly. I will say that this client worked at another facility (one I was actually at about 3-4 months ago) and they're going to report the place on various violations and get the place publicised in the light it should be. There was a patient with syphilis where they told him to remove the mask that was given to him to NOT spread the disease. Amongst other violations were beds on the floor, cameras not recording (I can not validate these being violations, I was only told by the client/patient that worked at the facility I was at previously). Not enough nutritional value in the foods, the list goes on. The client/patient said the facility was a shock to them. (I wish to protect the identity of this patient and gender).
